anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the Change on this case: the Exit check runs at D3 step 4 before any watch, the unchanged `open - needs src/guard.ts outside the diff` fires a concrete `stuck - needs ...` verdict (not Before's `fixable - 1 blocker` with a recommended ordinary fix row and a wait row), no watch, deadline, or implementer retry runs between the failed prerequisite and the report, and the obstacle menu is numeric deliver / assess / stop-recommended-last with the deliver row explicitly saying the retry happens only 'once that prerequisite changes', so the cap extension alone is not presented as clearing it. Nothing Before kept was lost (f2 holds in both). To keep this robust across sibling cases, keep the three-part shape of the deliver row ('resume retained course; retries P1 only when the prerequisite changes, no round charged; cumulative cap +2×maxFixRounds') rather than letting the cap-extension clause stand alone, keep the no-progress vs obstacle distinction wording ('not a no-progress exit because the iteration pushed a new head') since it explains why rounds_used is unchanged, and consider moving the `Not offered:` line and the evidence hint into the shared menus.md template verbatim so every scenario renders stop last and show-evidence hint-only identically.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the intended move on all three facts: step 2 applies the entry Exit check and converts the retained `open - needs src/guard.ts outside the diff` helper result into an explicit `stuck - needs ...` obstacle before any CI watch or implementer dispatch (f1), step 6 confirms no helper, watch, sync, or external write runs between that failed prerequisite and the rendered obstacle (f2), and the menu is the obstacle template with numeric deliver and assess, stop recommended and last, and no fix/wait rows (f3). Before fails all three because it treats the same helper result as an ordinary open blocker, renders `fixable - 1 blocker`, and offers wait/fix rows with fix recommended, so no obstacle report ever exists. Nothing regressed, so keep the After wording; one small tightening for f3 would be to state in the deliver row (or the Not offered line) that the cap extension by itself does not clear the failed prerequisite — currently that is implied by 'after the src/guard.ts prerequisite changes' plus step 2's 'I do not reinterpret it as permission to ... repeat the helper', but an explicit clause like 'extension alone does not clear this prerequisite' would remove any reader doubt.
